title: Separate and use partial fractions
text: Separate to get $$\frac{dy}{y \left(1+2y\right)}=2x$$ dx. Partial fractions give $$\frac{1}{y \left(1+2y\right)}=\frac{1}{y}-\frac{2}{1+2y}$$.

title: Integrate and solve
text: Integrating gives $$\ln\left(|\frac{y}{1+2y}|\right)=x^2+C$$ and at $$x=0$$ the fraction $$\frac{y}{1+2y}$$ equals $$1$$, so $$C=0$$ and $$\frac{y}{1+2y}=e^{x^2}$$. Solving for $$y$$ gives $$y=\frac{e^{x^2}}{1-2e^{x^2}}$$.
